${x_{1}^{′}(t) = x_{1}(t) + 3; x_{2}^{′}(t) =-x_{1}(t) + 3x_{2}(t),x(0) = \begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}$
Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables $X_{1}(s) = L{x_{1}(t)}$ and $X_{2}(s) = L{x_{2}(t)}$. In terms of the parameter $s$, the solution of the new system is$X_{1}(s) = (3 - 2s)/(s(s - 1))$,
$X_{2}(s) =$ {{field-1}}.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{2}(t)+4,\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

${X}_{2}(s)=\frac{2s+4}{s(s-3)}.$
